source_text: De vitiis quae opposita sunt virtutibus (sub nomine Nili Ancyrani) ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΛΟΓΟΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΤΟΝ ΑΥΤΟΝ ΠΕΡΙ ΤΑΣ ΑΝΤΙΖΥΓΟΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΑΡΕΤΩΝ ΚΑΚΙΑΣ. 79.1140 ΚΕΦΑΛ. Αʹ. Ἀναγκαῖον ἡγοῦμαι καὶ τὰς ἀντιζύγους τῶν ἀρετῶν κακίας δι' ἐπιτόμου ὑποτάξαι τῇ σῇ φιλοπονίᾳ· ἕως μὲν ὧδε τὴν διάνοιαν ἀροτριάσαντες, τὰς τῶν λογισμῶν ἀκάνθας ἐκ τῆς σπορίμου χώρας ἀνεβάλομεν· οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων δὲ, ἃ ἐποιήσαμεν ἡμεῖς εἰς τοῦτο παρεφθάσαμεν, ἀλλ' ὑποτύπωσιν ἔχοντες ὑγιαινόντων λόγων, ὧν ἠκούσαμεν, παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων, καί τινων τῶν πράξεων συνίστορες γεγενήμεθα. Τὸ δὲ πᾶν ἡ χάρις ἄνωθεν, ἡ καὶ τοῖς ἀμαρτωλοῖς ὑποδεικνύουσα τὰς τῶν φρεναπατῶν ἐπιβουλὰς, ἡ καὶ ἀσφαλιζομένη, καὶ λέγουσα· «Τί γὰρ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες;» ἵνα διὰ τοῦ λαβεῖν εὐχαριστῶμεν τῷ δεδωκότι, ὅτι μὴ ἑαυτοῖς ἀποδιδόαμεν καύχημά τι δόξης, τὴν δόσιν ἀρνούμενοι. διόπερ φησὶν, «Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες, τί καυχᾷ, ὡς μὴ λαβών;» –«Ἥδη, φησὶν, ἐπλουτήσατε» οἱ τοῖς ἔργοις πενόμενοι, ἤδη οἱ τοῦ διδάσκεσθαι ἀρξάμενοι, ἐκορέσθητε, ὧνπερ ἀρτίως ἡ πλάνη μεταβέβηκεν εἰς ἐμέ· δι' ἧς μὲν δεδάνεισμαι λογιστείας, τὴν τῶν ἔργων πενίαν παρακαλύπτων, δι' ἧς δὲ παρῄνεσα γνώμης τὴν τοῦ διδάσκεσθαι μαθητείαν ἀντιπεριτρέπων. Ἀλλ' ὅμως 79.1141 εἴ τις κεκράτηται παρ' ὑμῶν συγγνώμη, κἀμοὶ ταύτην ἀπονείματε, ἵνα καὶ τὰς ἀντιζύγους τῶν ἀρετῶν κακίας δι' ἐπιτόμου ὑποτάξωμεν σημαίνοντες· τί μέν ἐστι γαστριμαργία, καθ' ἧς ἐγκράτεια· τί δὲ πορνεία, καὶ σωφροσύνη· φιλαργυρία δὲ τί, καὶ ἀκτημοσύνη· λύπη, καθ' ἧς ἡ χαρά· ὀργὴ δὲ τί, καὶ μακροθυμία· καὶ ἀκηδία, καὶ ὑπομονή· τί δὲ κενοδοξία, καὶ ἀκενοδοξία, φθόνος, καὶ ἀφθονία, ὑπερηφανία, καὶ ταπείνωσις· ταῦτα ἀντίζυγα, καὶ ἀντίπαλα, καὶ ἀντίθετα ἀλλήλων ὅντα, δι' ἐπιτόμου οὕτως ὑπετάξαμεν. ΚΕΦΑΛ. Βʹ.
thought_title: Asking pardon to list vices matched to virtues
orientation: Evagrius opens by saying his teaching comes from grace and the Fathers, and he asks pardon before listing the vices paired with their virtues.
pass_a_gloss: Discourse of the same to the same concerning the vices paired against the virtues. Chapter 1. I consider it necessary also to set out in brief for your love of labor the vices paired against the virtues. Up to here having plowed the mind, we have cast out of the sown land the thorns of the thoughts. Not from works which we ourselves did have we come forward to this, but having a pattern of sound words which we heard from the Fathers, and we have become witnesses with knowledge of some of the deeds. And the whole is grace from above, the grace also pointing out to sinners the plots of the mind deceivers, the grace also making safe, and saying: For what do you have which you did not receive. In order that by the receiving we may give thanks to the one who gave, because we do not assign to ourselves any boast of glory, while denying the gift. For this reason it says: But if you also received, why do you boast as not having received. Already, it says, you became rich, you who are poor in works, already you who have begun to be taught were filled, you whose error just now has passed over into me. By which error on the one hand I have borrowed a reckoning, concealing the poverty of works, and by which counsel on the other hand I gave advice, turning round about the discipleship of being taught. But nevertheless, if any pardon is held in reserve by you, grant this also to me, in order that also the vices paired against the virtues we may set out in brief by signifying: what gluttony is, against which is self-control; what sexual immorality is, and chastity; what love of money is, and poverty; grief, against which is joy; what anger is, and patience; and listlessness, and endurance; what vainglory is, and freedom from vainglory; envy, and freedom from envy; pride, and humility. These being paired and matched and set over against each other, in brief thus we have set them out. Chapter 2.

pass_b_english: I hold it necessary to lay out briefly for your love of labor the vices paired against the virtues. Up to this point we have plowed the mind and thrown up the thorns of our thoughts out of the sown land. We have not come this far by works we ourselves have done. We hold a pattern of sound words we heard from the Fathers, and we have become witnesses to some of their practices.

The whole work is grace from above. Grace shows even to sinners the plots of the mind deceivers, and it guards us and speaks, saying, "What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7) It does this so that in receiving we may give thanks to the Giver, instead of assigning to ourselves any boast of glory by denying the gift. So grace says, "If you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?" (1 Corinthians 4:7) "You have already become rich," grace says (1 Corinthians 4:8) — you who are poor in works — "you have already had your fill," you who have only begun to be taught — whose delusion has just now passed over into me. Through it I have borrowed a reckoning that hides my poverty in works, and through the counsel I urged I have turned the learner's place of being taught on its head.

Still, if you keep any pardon in reserve, grant it to me as well, so that I may lay out briefly the vices paired against the virtues and show what each is: what gluttony is, and self-control set against it; what sexual immorality is, and chastity; what love of money is, and poverty; grief, and joy set against it; what anger is, and patience; listlessness, and endurance; what vainglory is, and freedom from vainglory; envy, and freedom from envy; pride, and humility. These stand paired against one another, contending and set over against one another, and in this brief form I have laid them out.

problems.quote: we who are poor in works — "you have already had your fill," we who have only begun to be taught. That delusion has just now passed over into me.
problems.source_quote: οἱ τοῖς ἔργοις πενόμενοι, ἤδη οἱ τοῦ διδάσκεσθαι ἀρξάμενοι, ἐκορέσθητε, ὧνπερ ἀρτίως ἡ πλάνη μεταβέβηκεν εἰς ἐμέ·
problems.why: The participles modify the second-person "you," not "we," and "ὧνπερ" means "whose," referring to those rebuked people whose delusion has now passed into Evagrius.
problems.fix: you who are poor in works — "you have already had your fill," you who have only begun to be taught — whose delusion has just now passed over into me.
problems.ruling: οἱ πενόμενοι/ἀρξάμενοι appositives to ἐπλουτήσατε/ἐκορέσθητε (you), not we; ὧνπερ whose delusion → ἐμέ
